When I was training to get my biggest I was training only four days a week and resting three days a week. There was a lot of work but this is what allowed me to get to my biggest. I was using all the compound movements for heavy weights like six to eight reps and I was resting three days a week. And then when you get older you need more recuperation too because the body doesn't recuperate as fast as it did when you were younger so the tendons and the joints need more rest. So I think the ideal training routine for older men and women is to train about four days a week as well. It's a mistake to do too much cardio, cardiovascular exercise. It's not going to build muscle tissue but it does help to burn off body fat. But doing it every day or doing too much cardio will tend to over train your body and it will actually prevent you from growing muscle tissue. When you do the weight training and you tear down muscle tissue you have to give your body enough time to recuperate. Doing cardio all the time is an exercise that will take up more energy and will burn up a lot of calories that you could be using to recuperate. I usually do around three maybe four days a week of cardio in the offseason. I'll only use around 30 minutes of cardio in each session. The time that you do the cardio is very important so I'll usually do the cardio first thing in the morning before I eat any food. This way I'm making sure that I'm burning stored body fat for energy. If I don't do it in the morning sometimes I'll do it after my workout after I've already burned off all my carbohydrates for my weight training. You never want to do cardio before you weight train because it's just going to burn energy that you could be using to lift weights. Walking is definitely considered cardio.
